author: Anne Marxze Umil
title: Not losing hope for 16 years, Mary Jane finally free
content:
Celia Veloso and Mary Jane. (Thomas Andrei Brecio/Pinoy Weekly)

Mary Jane’s release is historical for the overseas Filipino workers.

She was tired as seen in her puffy eyes. But her smile was evident upon being reunited with her loved ones after 16 years.

Finally, Mary Jane Veloso was released from prison.

“I’d like to eat pinakbet and inihaw na bangus,” Veloso replied to a reporter’s question about what she would eat once she is home in Nueva Ecija.

Aside from eating pinakbet, Veloso said that all she wanted was to take a rest.

Veloso was released from the Correctional Institute for Women (CIW) on the night of September 25 after Ferdinand Marcos Jr. granted her absolute pardon.

Veloso spent 16 years in prison, 15 years in Indonesia and a year and half at the CIW.

For Migrante International and National Union of Peoples’ Lawyers (among the groups that had led the fight for her freedom), Veloso should have been freed when she came back to the Philippines because she did not commit any crime in the country.

“Kung may tiyaga may nilaga,” Veloso said as she faced the media in a press conference on September 26. She thanked her family who did not leave her in her battle, as well as those who supported her and called on the government to grant her absolute pardon.

author: Martha Teodoro
title: Faith groups push against US-backed ‘Pax Silica’ hub
content:
Caritas Philippines President Bishop Gerardo Alminaza speaking at the press conference. (Photo by Martha Teodoro/Bulatlat)

Catholic bishops and Protestant leaders, Christian youth and environmental activists are joining forces to halt “Pax Silica,” an AI hub megaproject backed by the United States. Critics fear that this project would drain Central Luzon’s water and power supplies and displace Indigenous communities.

Inked in April 2026, “Pax Silica,” is a U.S.-led worldwide network aimed at protecting supply chains for computer chips, AI tech, and vital minerals. The Bases Conversion and Development Authority has set aside 1,620 hectares in New Clark City in Tarlac for this project, which will be an industrial district for mineral processing sites and automated data centers.

Government officials say the project will turn the Philippines into a worldwide tech powerhouse, but church groups and civil society organizations disagree.

Caritas Philippines President Bishop Gerardo Alminaza called on the national government not to make any binding guarantee all at once.

author: Davao Today
title: Students rally on Martial Law commemoration despite arrest threats
content:
“We should show that we are strong, that we are united here.”

On the 54th year of Martial Law imposition, students joined nationwide protests calling for remembrance, accountability and action.

They took to the streets despite heightened police presence and recent arrests of protesters.

For some students who joined the 54th anniversary commemoration of Martial Law on September 21, the possibility of arrest was not enough to keep them away from the streets. Instead, they said the risks reinforced the importance of being present.

For Alyssa (surname withheld), a Visual Communication student from the University of the Philippines Diliman College of Fine Arts, joining the commemoration was rooted in the right to speak and remember the victims of the dictatorship. “I think the reason why we are here is because even if there are activists being arrested, we should not be afraid to express our call because it is our right to speak.”

She said that the commemoration should not be reduced to a historical date, pointing to the victims of Martial Law and continuing concerns over the treatment of activists.

The National Capital Region Police Office placed Metro Manila on full alert, with more than 15,700 personnel deployed for the September 21 activities. Police said that the deployment was intended to maintain public safety while allowing peaceful assemblies.

author: Alyssa Mae Clarin
title: Gov’t grants Mary Jane Veloso absolute pardon after 16 years
content:
May Jane Veloso is welcomed by her family at the Correctional Institute for Women in Mandaluyong City, Dec. 18. (Photo by Deo Montesclaros/ Pinoy Weekly)

Veloso’s freedom was not granted voluntarily but was won through years of struggle by her family, lawyers, and supporters.

MANILA — Nearly two years since her return to the Philippines in December 2024, Mary Jane Veloso has been granted an absolute pardon by Ferdinand Marcos Jr., ending more than 16 years of detention stemming from a drug trafficking case in Indonesia.

“Pinirmahan ko na yung pardon niya kahapon,” (I already signed [the pardon] yesterday) Ferdinand Marcos Jr. told reporters during an interview in Eastern Samar.

The development came after Malacañang Press Officer Claire Castro said the president was “seriously considering” granting Veloso an absolute pardon. Veloso had been sentenced to death in Indonesia after authorities accused her of carrying 2.6 kilograms of heroin in 2010.

She was granted last-minute reprieve following international pressure on the Indonesian government.

Veloso’s lawyers from the National Union of Peoples’ Lawyers (NUPL) welcomed the decision, describing it as a “long-awaited act” that brings immeasurable relief to Veloso, her family, and the many supporters who stood by her throughout her years of detention.

title: Company seeks to evict Sebaring IP residents
content:
By Aurelia Solaba




The homes of the Cuyonon, Kagayanen, and Palaw’an indigenous residents of Barangay Sebaring, Bugsuk Island, Palawan have been at the mercy of changing tides not just from the flow of the seawater but also from the whims of a powerful company. 




Just like their neighbors in 

Sitio Marihangin

, the community is facing displacement because of ecotourism plans in the area. Unlike Sitio Marihangin, however, 

San Miguel Corporation

 has no direct involvement. 




Barangay Sebaring’s opponent is an entirely different enterprise, the Normal Holdings and Development Corporation.




Cycle of relocation




In 2018, the company purchased the mother title of Barangay Sebaring from the Gabinete family. The deal did not include the islanders’ homes but the corporation wants their land anyway.




Alex (not their real name), an ally of the islanders, said that the residents’ part of the barangay exists because 

“umurong yung dagat” 

(the sea receded) and the shoreline expanded. The newly formed beachfront was beyond their original ancestral domain which was the titled property of Honorio Gabinete and Pedro Gabinete. 




As a result, the community relocated to excess land now known as Lots 4625, 4626, and 4628.

author: Dominic Gutoman
title: ‘Human rights reparation starts with justice’
content:
Portraits of enforced disappearance victims. Photo by Dominic Gutoman/Bulatlat.

MANILA – All human rights violation victims should receive reparation consistent with domestic laws and international obligations.

“From a victim-oriented perspective, the State must recognize that different human rights violations may require various kinds of reparations based on the demands of the victims, their families, and communities which they belong to, to correct the wrongs and achieve healing,” the 2026 Commission on Human Rights (CHR) position paper stated. “Essentially, reparation should be proportional to the gravity of the violations committed and the extent of harm suffered.”

“When my daughter was killed, we received no single assistance nor investigation from the authorities. Not the barangay, not the police. Not one from the government offered help,” Sally Ramos told Bulatlat. Her daughter was killed in 2017 by four unidentified men at the height of the anti-drug campaign.

She said, “We are poor, I do not have a job. My daughter who was killed had a job before she was killed. She supported us for our daily needs and in taking care of my two grandchildren. That is why it was hard for me to accept her passing.”

author: Jian Sanz
title: CLSU Student Regent red-tagged in latest attack on student leaders
content:
Image of packaged sent to Balllesteros (photo from CLSU USSC)

Central Luzon State University Student Regent (CLSU SR) Rashela Ballesteros received a package containing red-tagging messages around 12:30 pm on September 17 at the University Supreme Student Council (USSC) office.

The package, sent by a certain Jared Mariano from Guimba, Nueva Ecija, contained a red-tagging message formatted as a love letter, an altered photo showing Ballesteros’s face pasted onto a soldier’s body, and a list of requirements to become an officer in the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP). The letter in the package read, “Hope I’ll see your smile in campus.(sic)”

In a statement, Anakbayan CLSU condemned yet another harassment and red-tagging of Ballesteros, reiterating that incidents like these result in serious violations of students’ rights to security and freedom of expression.

“This is a threat not only to SR Ballesteros, but also to the democratic rights of the entire CLSU community. It is crucial to protect the freedom of students to voice their demands and participate in social issues, both inside and outside the university,” the youth organization added.

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Rights groups assail military-led symposium redtagging progressives in Tacloban university
content:
Photo taken by an attendee during the symposium (name withheld for security reasons).

By Veronika Barbosa TACLOBAN CITY – Progressive groups in Eastern Visayas raised alarm over a red-tagging incident that happened last September 12, 2026 in a symposium led by the 8th Civil Military Operations “Dangpanan (CMO) Battalion inside the Leyte Normal University in Tacloban.

The attendees of the said symposium were students enrolled in the National Service Training Program (NSTP) course mostly composed of first-year students.

According to the accounts of some student attendees, an officer of the Armed Forces of the Philippines discouraged them from joining protest actions. “At first, he [the CMO officer] was only talking about the West Philippine Sea, then we were shocked that they started talking about terror grooming and how it is not necessary to criticize the government through mass mobilizations,” said Aya (name withheld for security reasons), an attendee of the symposium. author: Shan Kenshin Ecaldre
title: Impunity persists 54 years after martial law imposition
content:
Symbolic paper cranes were attached in a steel frame, holding the calls for the freedom of all political prisoners. Photo by Dominic Gutoman/Bulatlat.

“More than five decades have passed yet the painful legacy of martial law—human rights violations, injustice and lack of accountability—remains deeply entrenched.”

Fifty-four years after the declaration of martial law under the Marcos Sr. dictatorship, political prisoners stressed that abuses continue through corruption and the use of state institutions and laws against dissent.

The warning came from political prisoners detained at the Metro Manila District Jail Annex 4 in Bicutan. They issued a statement through KAPATID ahead of the September 21 commemoration of martial law.

Their statement came days after the Supreme Court overturned former First Lady Imelda Marcos’ 2018 Sandiganbayan conviction on seven counts of graft involving her alleged financial interests in private foundations in Switzerland.

The Supreme Court, in a decision dated June 10 but made public on September 9, acquitted Marcos after finding that prosecutors failed to establish her guilt beyond reasonable doubt. The court cited, among other issues, the failure to properly authenticate key Swiss documents and to establish that the foundations were “businesses” covered by the anti-graft law.

author: Reynard Magtoto
title: Bicol campus journalists, groups unite vs martial law distortion
content:
Standing for the Guild: CEGP Bicol participates in 54th ML protest in Legazpi City to demand press freedom. (Photo by Reynard Magtoto/Bulatlat)

“The martial law continues until now.”

“Martial Law, we will never forget. Defend press freedom.”

Various progressive groups stressed this point at their protest action in Legazpi City, Albay to commemorate the 54th year of Martial Law declaration on September 21.

Bayan Bicol, Condor-Piston Bicol, College Editors Guild of the Philippines (CEGP) Bicol, Kilusang Magbubukid ng Bicol (KMB), BUeños Kontra Korapsyon (BKK), Manibela Albay Chapter and other local groups marched from Bicol University (BU) main campus to Peñaranda Park, calling for accountability from the Marcos Jr. administration and urging Bicolanos to join their efforts against the distortion of martial law history.

“The Marcos family’s campaign of revisionism in Philippine history to erase the bloody and dark history of Martial Law must end,” Bayan Bicol Secretary-General Dan Balucio said. “Marcos Sr. was ousted but still a Marcos is the president today. The martial law continues until now.”

According to CEGP Bicol, the administration has changed but the media workers and campus journalists continue to face the dynastic rule of the Marcoses as they continue to plunder public funds for foreign interests while repressing rights to a free press.

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: News in pictures | US-wide campaign against Pax Silica launched
content:
NEW YORK – From the belly of the beast, resistance to the U.S.-initiated Pax Silica is rising.

The U.S.-wide launch of the Shut Down Pax Silica Campaign Network happened on Sunday, September 20 with over 500 people attending in New York City, online, and in watch parties all over the country. Convened by the International League of Peoples’ Struggle-US (ILPS-US), Bagong Alyansang Makabayan USA (BAYAN USA), and International Coalition for Human Rights in the Philippines-US (ICHRP-US), the network consists of 45 organizations who opposed the Pax Silica over impacts on environmental destruction and exploitation of the poor in other countries.

Speakers from Agham, Friends of the Congo, Countermapping Network PH, and Nodutdol shared about the impacts of AI and tech supply chains around the world, and the global threat of Pax Silica, with the Philippines as “ground zero” for the Initiative.

This event marked the beginning of the week of action at the UN General Assembly with the banner “No to War and Plunder, Fight for Peoples’ Rights, National Sovereignty, and Genuine Development.” (RVO)

author: Dominic Gutoman
title: Ombudsman dismisses human rights complaints vs military even without hearing
content:
Jhed Tamano and Jonila Castro. (Photo courtesy of Hands Off Jhed & Jonila Network)

Trigger warning: Description of state violence, torture, enforced disappearance

MANILA – For two years, not a single hearing was done on the torture and enforced disappearance complaints filed by environmental defenders Jonila Castro and Jhed Tamano against military officials before the Office of the Ombudsman. Despite this, the case was dismissed.

“Two years. No hearings. Then dismissal,” Kalikasan said in a statement. “Instead of reckoning with the evidence provided by the [victim] environmental defenders, the Ombudsman gave greater weight to the accounts of security officials and invoked the presumption of regularity in their favor.”

Tamano and Castro were affiliated with the Alyansa para sa Pagtatanggol sa Kabuhayan, Paninirahan, at Kalikasan ng Manila Bay (AKAP KA Manila Bay) when they were abducted on September 2, 2023 while conducting consultation and research with fishing communities affected by the Manila Bay reclamation projects.

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Groups remember Martial Law with protests
content:
homas Andrei Brecio at Jeoff Larua /Pinoy Weekly

MANILA — “We shall never forget.”

Progressive groups announced on September 15 its planned protest actions on September 21 to commemorate the 54th anniversary of the declaration of Martial Law and to press the government for accountability over corruption, particularly the controversy surrounding flood control projects.

The Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan) said that it will join the Kilusang Bayan Kontra Kurakot (KBKK) rally at Liwasang Bonifacio in the afternoon before leading a march to Mendiola.

Bayan said that the mobilization pays tribute to the Filipino people’s resistance to the dictatorship of the late dictator Ferdinand Marcos Sr. while continuing calls for accountability over the flood control controversy that sparked large anti-corruption protests last year.

The group said that the protest should also be a reminder of the continuing problems of poverty, corruption, repression, and foreign influence.

Bayan stressed that the Marcos Sr. dictatorship was marked by state violence, political repression, corruption and cronyism. The Marcos Jr. administration, Bayan said, implemented similar policies through continued political harassment and expanded cooperation with the United States.

author: Danilo Arao
title: F2F
content:
Classrooms in Batasan National High School in Quezon City is divided into two rooms to accommodate more students. (Photo grabbed from ACT Teachers Party Facebook page)

Huwag sisihin ang malakas na pag-ulan dahil may mas malaking kasalanan ang palpak na pamahalaan.

Ilang beses na bang nagkaroon ng suspensiyon sa klase dahil sa malakas na pag-ulan?

Mula sa personal na karanasan, nagsimula na ang klase sa Unibersidad ng Pilipinas (UP) at Politeknikong Unibersidad ng Pilipinas (PUP) noong Agosto pero isang beses pa lang naisasagawa ang face-to-face (F2F) na klase sa isang kurso. Dalawang beses o higit pa sa iba pang kurso pero siyempre’y mas madalas ang asynchronous at synchronous (online) na mga sesyon.

At sa mangilan-ngilang pagkakataong may F2F na klase, may mga estudyanteng nale-late o lumiliban. Nahihirapang bumiyahe papuntang kampus, binabaha ang lugar o nagkakasakit dahil naulanan—mahaba pa ang listahan ng mga paliwanag. Malinaw na nahihirapan ang marami, lalo na ang mga kapos sa buhay!

Kumusta naman ang kalagayan ng anak na nag-aaral sa UP Integrated School (UPIS)? Habang sinusulat ito, hindi pa siya nakakapaglaro ng table tennis dahil parating suspendido ang F2F na klase sa mismong araw ng Physical Education (PE). Hindi man sayang ang mga biniling paddle at bola, nakalulungkot lang na hindi pa niya nagagamit ang mga ito.

Siyempre’y higit na nakalulungkot ang dumarami

Simulan natin ang pagninilay sa tanong ni Pedro kay Hesus: “Panginoon, ilang beses ko po ba dapat patawarin ang aking kapatid na nagkakasala sa akin? Hanggang pitong beses po ba?” Sa kultura at tradisyon noong panahon na iyon, ang magpatawad ng tatlong beses ay itinuturing nang higit pa sa sapat. Kaya naman sa pag-aalok ni Pedro ng pitong beses, akala niya ay napakarami at napakarangal na ng kanyang mungkahi. Ngunit pinalawak ni Hesus ang hangganan ng pag-unawa ng tao. author: Dominic Gutoman
title: Martial law survivors enraged by SC’s reversal of Imelda Marcos graft conviction
content:
“It spits in the face of the victims of human rights violations whose lives were robbed while the Marcoses lived an extravagant lifestyle.”

MANILA – The Supreme Court (SC) has reversed Imelda Marcos’s convictions in seven graft cases. For martial law survivors, the decision is a spit in the face of the victims.

“Her acquittal is one of the gravest blows to the decades-long struggle for justice and accountability for the massive plunder attributed to the Marcos dictatorship,” Samahan ng Ex-Detainees Laban sa Detensyon at Aresto (Selda), an organization that led the efforts on the historic class suit against the dictator Marcos Sr. in Hawaii, noted in a joint statement with human rights group Karapatan.

The decision of the high court acquitted Marcos of graft charges due to reported failure of the prosecution to prove her guilt beyond reasonable doubt.

“It spits in the face of the victims of human rights violations whose lives were robbed while the Marcoses lived an extravagant lifestyle,” the groups added.

“This is how hollow justice can be in a country where those accused and convicted of plunder continue to evade accountability, while ordinary Filipinos are made to bear the cost of corruption and the big-time robbery of public funds.”

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Groups in Eastern Visayas welcome arrest of Romualdez
content:
“While the Romualdezes are reveling in their stolen wealth, the people of Eastern Visayas struggle with extreme food insecurity.”

TACLOBAN CITY – Progressive groups from Eastern Visayas welcomed the arrest of Leyte First District Representative and former House Speaker Ferdinand Martin Romualdez over charges of plunder.

In a statement, Bagong Alyansang Makayan (Bayan) Sinirangan Bisayas considered Romualdez’s arrest as a win for the Filipino people. “It’s been a year since we have incessantly marched the streets to protest the widespread corruption and finally, key players of ghost flood control projects like Romualdez are now being held accountable.”

While the group welcomed the warrants of arrest issued to Martin Romualdez and former Ako Bicol Representative Zaldy Co, they said that the magnitude of such corruption extends beyond Co and Romualdez and could have not been carried out by only two or four individuals. “The testimonies and revelations of Co and DPWH Undersecretary Roberto Bernardo points to a much wider network of officials involved. Most seriously, Ferdinand Marcos Jr. tolerated and benefited from the scheme,” Bayan Alyansang Makabayan said in a statement.
